outcome: Let values the agent holds enter as a dataset (GAPS G4): import_dataset accepts rows written inline, a list of objects with a name, in place of a path; they are kept as a content-addressed JSON source in the workspace and imported through the same path as a file, so a literal answer or a reading of a document, image or video has provenance without a raw_query that pretends to read the source.
criteria: Backend.import_dataset and the MCP import_dataset tool accept rows (a non-empty list of objects whose values are text, numbers, booleans or null) together with name, instead of path; the rows are written to a content-addressed JSON file under the workspace, registered as an artifact marked as inline rows, and imported with the file path's type inference, temporal refinement, provenance, audit and idempotent replay of identical rows under the same name (tested).
Refusals name the accepted shape for neither or both of path and rows, rows without a name, empty rows, a row that is not an object, and a nested value in a row.

A transform whose source is written as a list of flat row objects is advised with a rewrite that imports them with import_dataset(rows=..., name=...) and runs the transform on that name, and a raw_query refused as source_unused that reads no dataset at all names import_dataset rows; rewrites sent back succeed (tested).

The import_dataset tool description and README.md say that rows are how values the agent read or computed outside the backend enter it; MADR 0009 and MADR 0008 carry Decision History entries recording the decision and the alternatives set aside (a separate tool, a raw_query over VALUES).
The tests use data unrelated to any benchmark, the boundary test still passes, and the full test suite passes.

dispositions.note: import_dataset(rows=..., name='Tide readings') imports 3 rows as tide_readings with string/float/date/boolean/string columns (the ISO dates refined), missing keys as null; the rows are one content-addressed JSON file under the workspace's files/, the artifact is named 'rows written inline' with metadata origin inline_rows, the operation intent records count, columns and artifact id, and the same rows and name replay the original operation. Also through MCP, whose schema no longer requires path.

INVALID_INTENT with field and the rows shape as hint for neither path nor rows, rows without name, empty rows, a non-object row, a nested value, a non-finite number, and both path and rows; format or table with rows is refused as describing a file.

a transform whose source is a list of flat row objects gets source_as_dataset with the rewrite import_dataset(rows, name='inline_rows') then the transform on inline_rows, which run and return the filtered row; a single row object is explained without a rewrite; a raw_query of VALUES refused as source_unused names import_dataset(rows=...).

the import_dataset tool description, README (the boundary paragraph, an example call, the implemented table) and the AGENTS.md module map describe rows written inline; MADR 0009 and 0008 carry 2026-09-25 history entries naming the alternatives set aside.
tests use tide readings, weighed lots and an invented answer row; the boundary test passes; 414 passed, 8 skipped.

note: Imported datasets usually take their source file's stem as an alias; rows written inline share one artifact name, so they take none. A column that is null in every row is typed unknown, as DuckDB reads it. No size limit is set on rows.
